method: nearest class centroid; means from 1000 training records (200 per class), test on the 500-record semantic holdout
interpretation: The sparse winner-take-all code is more linearly separable than the raw features (0.420 vs 0.300) and than the dense expansion (0.332). A trivial nearest-centroid readout on the sparse code matches the gradient-trained raw linear head (Q3.4/Q3.6 linear anchor: 0.416). The representation is therefore not the cause of the Q3.5/Q3.6 expanded-head failure, and the fixed sparse random expansion does not exceed the raw features' linear-semantic ceiling. This is exploratory and made no scientific decision.
